title: Introducing yourself
summary: Name, age, where you're from, where you live, job and hobbies — formal (Sie) and informal (du).
phrases: What do you do for a living? |
What do you like doing in your free time? |
lines: Hi everyone! A warm welcome to "Daily German Talk"!
Hi! How are you all? We're happy you're here.
I'm Anna.
And I'm Ben.
So Ben, how are you today?
I'm very well, thanks. And you, Anna?
I'm great. I had coffee this morning. Very important!
Oh yes, coffee is super important. What did you do at the weekend?
On Saturday I was in the park. The weather was nice. And you?
I was lazy. I read a book at home and listened to music.
That sounds very nice too. Relaxing is good.
Okay, let's start with the topic. Anna, how do you introduce yourself? What do you say first?
Very simple. First you say "Hallo" or "Guten Tag". Then you say your name. For example: "Hallo, ich bin Anna."
"Hallo, ich bin Ben."
That's easy.
Very good. You can also say: "Mein Name ist Anna." That's a little more formal. "Mein Name ist Ben." Formal, like at the office?
Yes, exactly! With a boss or at school. "Hallo, ich bin..." is friendly and relaxed, the way we're talking here now.
Perfect! And after the name, what comes next?
Often you say where you're from. "Ich komme aus..." For example: "Ich komme aus Deutschland."
"Ich komme aus Österreich." *wink* No, just kidding! I'm from Germany too.
Ben, be honest! So: "Ich komme aus Berlin" or "Ich komme aus Köln."
Got it. And what about "wohnen"? "Ich wohne in..."?
Yes, that's very important too. "Ich wohne in München" or "Ich wohne in Hamburg."
So: "Ich wohne in Frankfurt." Is that right?
Yes, that's right! You're being creative today.
Okay, okay. I really live in Berlin. So: name, origin, place you live. What else?
Maybe your job. "Ich bin Lehrerin" or "Ich bin Student."
And I'm... I'm an artist. No, I'm a teacher too.
Ben is a very funny teacher, I think.
Thanks! So, let's practise all of that together. Please introduce yourself to me, Anna.
Gladly. Breathe in deeply, speak slowly and clearly. "Hello, I'm Anna. I'm from Bremen, but now I live in Berlin. I'm a German teacher. And you?"
Very nice! Now me: "Good afternoon, my name is Ben Schmidt. I'm from Berlin and I live here too. I'm a teacher and I really like coffee."
We know that! Great! Now let's do a little situation. Imagine we're at a party. We don't know each other.
Ah, a party, okay. Hi!
Hi! I'm Anna. And you?
I'm Ben. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you. That's an important phrase, guys: "Schön dich kennenzulernen" or formally: "Schön Sie kennenzulernen."
Yes, "Schön dich kennenzulernen." Where are you from, Anna?
I'm from Bremen. And you, Ben, are you from Berlin?
Yes, exactly. I'm from Berlin. I live here in Prenzlauer Berg.
Oh, cool! I live in Prenzlauer Berg too. What do you do for a living?
I'm a teacher. I teach art. And you?
I'm a teacher too. I teach German. We have a lot in common.
Really? That's funny. Do you like music?
Yes, I like music a lot. I like listening to pop music, and you?
I like jazz and I play a bit of guitar.
Wow, that's great! So, now we know each other better.
Yes, that was a good conversation. Now let's do another situation. Maybe at school with a new student, more formal.
Good idea! You're the teacher, Ben, I'm a new student. My name is... Luka.
Good morning! You're new here, right?
Yes, exactly. Good morning! My name is Luka Meyer. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you! I'm Ben Schmidt, your teacher. Where are you from, Mr Meyer?
I'm from Switzerland, from Zurich.
Oh, from Switzerland! Welcome to Berlin! Where do you live now?
I live in Mitte, near Alexanderplatz.
That's very central, that's good. What do you do? Are you a student?
Yes, I'm a student. I study computer science.
Very interesting! Good luck in Berlin!
Thank you very much, Mr Schmidt.
Phew, being formal is exhausting!
But you were very good. You see, viewers: "Sie" for formal, "du" for friendly.
Important! Now a question: how do you say "How old are you?"?
Ah, that's: "Wie alt bist du?" Or formally: "Wie alt sind Sie?"
And the answer: "Ich bin..."?
Exactly! "Ich bin 30 Jahre alt" or just "Ich bin 30."
Well, I'm 25 years old. A dream!
Ben, you're at least 30! Set a good example!
Okay, okay. I'm 32 years old. And you, Anna?
I'm 28. So, now we know that too.
What else can you ask? Maybe about hobbies?
Yes: "Was sind deine Hobbys?" or "Was machst du gern in deiner Freizeit?"
My hobbies are reading and listening to music, and I like cooking.
Oh, that's great. I don't like cooking, I like eating! My hobbies are travelling and watching films.
Travelling is great. Where do you like to travel?
I like travelling to Italy. I love the food and the weather.
I like travelling to Scandinavia. I like the nature.
Very nice! So, now let's introduce ourselves once more completely, with all the information, for the viewers to say along.

Perfect idea! I'll start. I'll speak slowly and clearly, with small pauses: "Hello, my name is Ben Schmidt. I'm 32 years old. I'm from Berlin and I live here too. I'm a teacher. My hobbies are reading, music and cooking. Nice to meet you."

Nice to meet you too! Great, Ben! Now me: "Good afternoon, my name is Anna Weber. I'm 28 years old. I'm from Bremen, but now I live in Berlin. I'm a German teacher. In my free time I like travelling and I watch films. Nice to meet you."
Wonderful! That was a complete "Selbstgespräch"!
Introducing yourself, not a Selbstgespräch! A Selbstgespräch is when you talk to yourself.
Ah, sorry! Introducing yourself. Now our viewers can introduce themselves too.
Exactly, you can practise this! Talk with us! Say your name, where you're from, what you do...
Don't be afraid, start slowly! "Hallo, ich bin..." and your name. That's a great start.
Absolutely! So, we still have a little time. Let's play a game!
A game? What kind of game?
We introduce ourselves, but with wrong information. The viewers have to find the mistake.

Oh, that's fun! Okay, I'll start. I'll try to look serious: "Hello, I'm Vladimir. I'm from Australia. I live in a small village. I'm a pilot. I'm 100 years old. My hobbies are skateboarding and video games."
Ben, that's all wrong! You're not Vladimir, you're Ben! You're not from Australia and you're not 100 years old!
Okay, maybe that was too obvious. Your turn!
Okay, listen! I'll speak in a normal voice: "Good afternoon, I'm Sophie. I'm from Vienna in Austria. I live in a big house. I'm a doctor. I'm 40 years old. I like swimming and dancing."
Hmm, that sounds almost right! But your name isn't Sophie, it's Anna! And you're not from Vienna and you're not 40!
Right, very well spotted! That one was harder.
That was fun! Now our viewers know how to introduce themselves.
Exactly, you can practise this. Talk with us, say your name, where you're from, what you do.
Don't be afraid, start slowly: "Hallo, ich bin..." and your name. That's a great start.
So Ben, today we talked a lot about introducing yourself.
Yes, that's right. Now it's time for our mini vocabulary training. We'll repeat the most important words and sentences.
Exactly, guys! Grab a tea or coffee, get comfortable and repeat with us!
Our first and most important word is: "sich vorstellen". Let me say it slowly: "sich vor-stel-len". Anna, what does it mean?
"Sich vorstellen" means "to introduce oneself". It's a reflexive verb. That sounds complicated, but it just means you do it to yourself. "I introduce myself" -> "Ich stelle mich vor."
And "Ich stelle mich vor" and "Wir stellen uns vor". Can you use the word in another way too?
Yes, but careful! "Sich etwas vorstellen" can also mean "to imagine something". For example: "Stell dir vor, wir fliegen nach Bali!" ("Imagine we fly to Bali!")
Oh yes, "Imagine I can fly!"
Ben, you're such an odd bird! But for today we only mean "sich vorstellen" for introductions. So guys, repeat after us: "sich vorstellen".
Very good! The next very, very important word: "der Name".
"Der Name", that's easy: "name". "My name is Ben" -> "Mein Name ist Ben." Right! And how do you ask about it?
"Wie heißt du?" That's the friendly question, or formally: "Wie heißen Sie?"
Perfect! And the answer is: "Ich heiße Anna" or "Mein Name ist Anna." Both are correct. Say it with us: "Wie heißt du?" And now: "Mein Name ist..."
Okay, next big point: "woher kommen" and "wo wohnen". That's sometimes tricky.
Yes, let's explain it! "Woher kommst du?" ("Where are you from?") That's your origin. "Ich komme aus Deutschland", "Ich komme aus Spanien."
And "Wo wohnst du?" ("Where do you live?") That's your current address. "Ich wohne in Berlin", "Ich wohne in München." Often it's the same, but not always.
Good example, Ben, you say it!
So: "Ich komme aus Berlin und ich wohne in Berlin." Everything in one place.
And me: "Ich komme aus Bremen, aber ich wohne in Berlin." Two different places. Do you see the difference?
Let's practise! Anna, where are you from?
I'm from Bremen. Ben, where do you live?
I live in Berlin.
Great! So viewers, your turn! Ask yourself: "Woher komme ich?" and answer: "Ich komme aus..." And then: "Wo wohne ich?" -> "Ich wohne in..."
Now a word for work: "beruflich". "Was machst du beruflich?"
That means "What do you do for a living?" or "What's your job?"
And the answer always starts with: "Ich bin..." ("I am..."). Anna, what do you do for a living?
I'm a teacher. And you, Ben?
I'm a teacher. We can also say: "Ich bin Student", "Ich bin Arzt", "Ich bin Kellnerin", "Ich bin Ingenieur."
Important: female job titles often end in "-in": "Lehrer" -> "Lehrerin", "Arzt" -> "Ärztin".
Right! So guys, what do you do for a living? Say: "Ich bin..."
So, now it gets more exciting: the word "das Hobby". The plural is "die Hobbys".
"Das Hobby", very easy, it's just like in English. "Was sind deine Hobbys?"
Or you can ask: "Was machst du gern in deiner Freizeit?" ("What do you like to do in your free time?")
My hobbies are reading and listening to music, and I like cooking. Anna, what are your hobbies?
My hobbies are travelling and watching films, and I like swimming.
Okay viewers, now it's your turn! What are your hobbies? Say three sentences: "Meine Hobbys sind... und ich... gern." For example: "Meine Hobbys sind Lesen und Sport, und ich koche gern."
We learned a new word today: "das Alter" ("the age").
How do you ask about it?
"Wie alt bist du?" (friendly) or "Wie alt sind Sie?" (formal).
And the answer is: "Ich bin... Jahre alt" or just "Ich bin 30."
Careful with the numbers, they're sometimes strange: not "twenty-five" but "fünfundzwanzig" ("five and twenty").
Exactly! "Ich bin 28" and "Ben ist 32." So guys, how old are you? Say: "Ich bin... Jahre alt."
Now let's do a little challenge! I'll say a word in English and you, Ben, say it in German, okay?
Okay, I'm ready!
First word: "To introduce oneself".
That's "sich vorstellen", not hard!
Very good! Next: "Where do you live?"
"Wo wohnst du?" or "Wo wohnen Sie?"
Perfect! Next: "Job".
Hmm, "der Beruf" or "Was machst du beruflich?"
Great! Last one: "Hobbies".
"Die Hobbys", easy!
You're the best, Ben! So viewers, can you do it too? Give it a try!
Now let's do the opposite: I say it in German and you say it in English, or our viewers say it in their heads.
Let's do it!
First word: "woher kommen".
"Where are you from?", easy!
Next: "Ich bin Studentin."
"I am a student (female)."
Very nice! Last one: "Schön dich kennenzulernen."
"Nice to meet you!" That's the most important thing at the end! Wow, that was a lot of vocabulary! Let's quickly repeat it all together.
Let's recap: that was "sich vorstellen", "der Name", "wohnen"...
..."kommen aus"...
..."beruflich"...
..."das Hobby"...
..."das Alter"...
...and the most important sentence: "Schön dich kennenzulernen!" So, that was a lot today. We learned how to introduce ourselves completely.
Yes, with name, age, origin, place you live, job and hobbies. You can now have a whole conversation!
Exactly! Now it's time for the question of the day. And today the question is very easy, because you know all the words.
What's your name, where are you from and what is your favourite hobby?
That means: "What's your name?", "Where are you from?" and "What is your favorite hobby?"
Please, please write your answer in the comments below, we want to get to know you all!
For example, write: "Hello, I'm Maria. I'm from Italy. My favourite hobby is dancing."
Or: "Good afternoon, my name is Tom. I'm from Canada. My favourite hobby is football."
We read all the comments and reply. We're looking forward to it!
Thank you so much for being here today! You did great!
Take care, keep practising and see you next time!
topics: Introduce yourself: name, where you're from, where you live, job
Your weekend: where were you, what did you do, what was the weather like?
Hobbies and free time: what do you like, what do you play?
Job and work: what do you do, where do you work, how is your job?

focus.title: Conjugating heißen
points: To say your name: Ich heiße Anna. — to ask: Wie heißt du? (informal) / Wie heißen Sie? (formal)
Present tense: ich heiße · du heißt · er/sie heißt · wir heißen · ihr heißt · Sie heißen
The stem ends in ß, so with du it only adds -t: du heißt (not heißst)
Other ways: Ich bin Anna. (casual) · Mein Name ist Anna. (more formal)

focus.title: Formal ↔ informal
points: du for friends, family, children and people your age — Sie (always with a capital S) for strangers, at work and for older people
With Sie the verb is conjugated like the plural: Woher kommen Sie? — with du: Woher kommst du?
The possessive changes too: dein Name ↔ Ihr Name
When you meet someone: Schön dich kennenzulernen ↔ Schön Sie kennenzulernen

focus.title: Where you're from
points: Origin uses aus, and aus always takes the Dativ: Ich komme aus Berlin.
Most countries and cities have no article: aus Deutschland, aus Zürich
Some countries have an article, and it changes in the Dativ: die Schweiz → aus der Schweiz · der Iran → aus dem Iran · die USA → aus den USA
Question: Woher kommst du? — short answer: Aus Bremen.

focus.title: Where you live
points: Where you live is in + Dativ: Ich wohne in Berlin. · Ich wohne in der Schweiz.
Ask with wo (where?): Wo wohnst du? — compare woher (where from?) and wohin (where to?)
Contraction: in + dem = im: im Zentrum, im Dorf
wohnen is regular: ich wohne · du wohnst · er wohnt · wir wohnen

focus.title: Saying your job (no article)
points: Jobs come without an article: Ich bin Lehrer. (not ein Lehrer)
For women you usually add -in: Lehrer → Lehrerin · Student → Studentin · Arzt → Ärztin
Question: Was machst du beruflich? / Was bist du von Beruf?
If you study: Ich studiere Informatik.
